baseline: Genuinely earned saved run continued through Wave4 with visible controls, earned recruitment and material costs; source save is not redistributed.

live.method: Fresh browser contexts from the same saved state; only ballista policy changed through visible controls. Real-time frames, no grants, no manual aid in the comparison. Separate one-input audit validates the local manual-hit path.

diagnostics.method: Diagnostic replay of the combat starting conditions observed from a genuinely earned Wave5 save. Same units, keys, positions, stats, encounter token, cooldowns, camp and fixed 1/30 dt. Only ballista policy differs. No manual aid. This is not a new earned playthrough.

conclusions: In this Wave5 lineup, changing only ballista policy does not change the fixed-dt attacks or outcome. Both live policies also lose with nine kills and five escapes.
All five survivors in the fixed-dt Wave5 diagnostic are on the upper road; the lower road is cleared.
The single preselected alternate Wave4 diagnostic also has no ballista policy-choice opportunities and the same result under both policies. It is not an earned Wave4 replay.
An exposed manual-input audit records one attempt and the real applied HP loss, without double-crediting it to a squad.
Policy choice is conditional on eligible in-range targets; this result does not establish that the priority is globally useful or useless.
limitations: Only this earned formation and one preselected alternate wave were evaluated.
Live frame intervals differ; fixed-dt comparisons isolate policy while browser trials validate actual code and UI.

Preparation clocks, journey timers, production cooldowns and inactive entry timestamps are excluded from equality checks because they are not combat inputs; a first overly broad equality check was corrected after it flagged these expected wall-clock differences.
Killed-target projectiles and overkill are not credited as applied contribution. No new visible statistics, rewards, balance multipliers or automatic placement are added.
